📌 Prediction Markets: Trading on Future Events

Main Points
⏺ Prediction markets let you trade on the outcome of events like elections, sports, or crypto decisions
⏺ Prices act like probabilities, showing what the crowd “thinks” will happen
⏺ This post explains how prediction markets turn opinions into tradable assets

1️⃣ Core Idea — instead of just guessing who will win, you buy “Yes” or “No” shares tied to a specific outcome
2️⃣ Pricing — if a “Yes” share trades at $0.70, the market is roughly saying there’s a 70% chance of that result
3️⃣ Settlement — after the event, winning shares pay out $1 while losing ones go to zero
4️⃣ Use Cases — forecasting politics, economic data, protocol decisions, and even on-chain governance outcomes
5️⃣ Signal Power — because people risk real money, prediction markets can sometimes be more accurate than polls or surveys

Final Thoughts

Prediction markets turn beliefs into positions — the stronger your conviction, the more you’re willing to back it with real capital.

📌 How will ESMA supervise crypto firms under MiCA in 2027? 

📣 The European Securities and Markets Authority has set operational resilience, outsourcing and sufficient EU based operations among its main crypto supervisory priorities for 2027 as the bloc moves further into enforcement of the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation. 

🌐 ESMA said in its 2027 work program published Monday that its work on MiCA will concentrate on coordinating national regulators and developing more consistent supervision of crypto asset service providers across the European Union. The program comes as the regulator moves from writing and implementing MiCA rules toward overseeing how licensed firms comply with them in practice.  Chair Verena Ross described the change during a meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, saying ESMA’s MiCA work had moved “from rulemaking towards supervision and convergence.” 

⭐️ Operational resilience will be one of the main areas under scrutiny as ESMA works with national competent authorities responsible for supervising CASPs. Outsourcing risks, liquidity, reverse solicitation and the classification of crypto assets are among the other areas identified for coordinated work in 2027. Supervisors will pay attention to whether firms maintain sufficient operations within the EU instead of relying heavily on functions or infrastructure based elsewhere.

Hegseth’s Execution Livestream Order Catches the Army Off Guard, Triggering a Political Firestorm

A decision announced by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has sent shockwaves through the Pentagon, raising urgent questions about military leadership, the psychological toll on American service members, and the limits of turning the machinery of justice into a public spectacle.

Hegseth’s announcement that the execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan would be livestreamed reportedly caught senior Army and Pentagon officials off guard. 

According to sources familiar with the discussions, many military officials first learned of the plan when Hegseth revealed it during a Wednesday interview aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.

The announcement immediately set off a series of difficult questions: Who would carry out the execution? How would the broadcast be conducted? And what consequences could the decision have for the soldiers ordered to participate?

Hasan was convicted for the 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, that killed 13 people and wounded more than 30 others. His scheduled execution by firing squad, expected to take place at Fort Hood on December 3, would mark an extraordinary moment in the modern history of American military justice.

But the proposed livestream has transformed the case into a broader national controversy.

Hegseth has defended the decision as a way to demonstrate that serious crimes carry serious consequences. Yet the prospect of broadcasting a military execution to a potentially worldwide audience has drawn criticism from both sides of the political aisle.

For some military personnel, the controversy extends far beyond the punishment itself. The central concern is what happens to the people ordered to carry it out — and whether the public exposure of such an act could leave lasting psychological scars.

📣 Japan arrests two suspect over 81M yen crypto police scam 

🔖 Japanese police have arrested two people suspected of helping a fake police fraud group steal cryptocurrency worth approximately 81 million yen from a woman in her 40s. The victim was allegedly told that her bank card had been connected to a large money laundering investigation. According to police information cited by FNN, the group claimed a fraud case had caused 600 billion yen in losses and that around 400 accounts had been used to launder funds.

⚠️ FNN reported that the caller told the woman her card appeared among accounts connected with the supposed money laundering investigation. The caller then claimed she was close to being arrested and needed to “prove her innocence.” Police allege that the false accusation eventually led the victim to transfer cryptocurrency worth around 81 million yen. The assets were valued at approximately $515,000 using the conversion cited in reports on the case.

‼️ Investigators have not publicly identified the cryptocurrencies involved or disclosed the wallet addresses that received the assets. Available reporting therefore does not establish how the cryptocurrency was subsequently moved, converted or withdrawn. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department believes Okayama and Minamisawa participated in a larger organization. Known losses from fraud cases involving the two suspects have reached approximately 240 million yen, according to FNN.

Weather modification technology is real and documented, going back decades. The question isn’t whether people can decide to influence weather. The question is whether they are.

At some point you start connecting the dots. Floods, fires, storms, it keeps coming, and something just doesn’t sit right...

So asking you again, what do you think is really going on?
